solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Couldn't decide on the spot — did sandwiches

indicators.note: the word did is wrapped round another piece like bread round a filling

parts.note: being on the spot means being there, present

explanation.surface: Someone who wavered at the crucial moment, pictured making sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is the container signal, the verb meaning wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate, unable to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Fears silly dear's coming to bad end

indicators.note: end picks out the final letter of the word bad
silly suggests the letters behaving foolishly and falling out of order

explanation.surface: Worries that a foolish loved one will meet a sorry fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges DEARS; 'end' takes D, the last letter of 'bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreads, as a verb, means fears greatly.

clue.text: Whose is the one with vacant rooms?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so only the outer letters of rooms remain

explanation.surface: A question about a guest house with free rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties 'rooms' to RS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked whose something is, the reply can be that it belongs to them.

clue.text: Fallen idol always held to be a baddie

indicators.note: held means kept within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: fallen suggests a toppled idol, its letters lying in a new order

explanation.surface: A disgraced hero now permanently regarded as a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fallen' (the toppled idol of the surface) signals the anagram, giving ILDO; 'held' is the container signal, and the answer's hyphen does not fall where the pieces join.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is a wrongdoer, a villain.

clue.text: Returning in almost no time flat

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the remaining letters are read backwards
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: never means at no time

explanation.surface: Coming back home to a flat in hardly any time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts NEVER to NEVE, which 'Returning' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level, smooth, with no bumps.

clue.text: Sounded hurt and deeply upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of deeply are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cried out in pain and was genuinely distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deeply' looks like an adverb on 'upset'; its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelp is a sharp cry of pain, so to have yelped is to have sounded hurt.

clue.text: Polishes pieces editor's chosen for cover

indicators.note: picked to cover, so the letters go round another piece

parts.note: ED is an editor, and the possessive adds the S
chessmen are the pieces in a game

explanation.surface: An editor tidies up the articles picked for the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' suggests newspaper articles, but they are chessmen; 'chosen for cover' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it.

clue.text: As usual, name's misspelt, it's kind of Italian

parts.note: par is the normal level, as in on a par

indicators.note: misspelt means the letters are written in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone's name gets mangled yet again, Italian style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misspelt' rearranges NAMES to MESAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese, so it is one kind of Italian food.

clue.text: No, I don't bother to include a gift

indicators.note: to include means to take in, so the shuffled letters go round a piece
bother as in disturb, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone declining to put in a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bother' rearranges NOIDONT, and 'to include' places A among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, usually to a charity.

clue.text: Observe craft used in women's make-up

parts.note: to eye something is to observe it
a liner is a large ocean-going craft

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch a technique applied in cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is a cosmetic drawn along the lash line, part of a make-up kit.

clue.text: Among non-Euro nations, one of many you have in mind

definitions.text: one of many you have in mind

indicators.note: among tells us the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something one has in common with countries outside the eurozone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' hides the answer across nON-EURO Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve cells are the brain's units, and there are billions of them in your mind.

clue.text: Goes off salesman's arrogance

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
putting on airs is behaving arrogantly

explanation.surface: A salesman's swagger turns people off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes off' looks like spoiling, but is to repair, an old verb for go.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is a formal way of saying to go off there.

clue.text: Laugh at eider duck's first flying

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word duck
flying suggests the letters taking off and settling in another order

explanation.surface: Mocking a sea duck as it takes to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges EIDER plus D, the first letter of 'duck'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule someone.

clue.text: Tired of graveyard patrol?

definitions.meaning: a beat among the dead, a watchman's round of a cemetery

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into a policeman's beat and the dead it passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead beat is an idiom for completely exhausted, and a beat among the dead suits a graveyard.

clue.text: The man's concealing irritation for things going awry

indicators.note: concealing means hiding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: he's is the man is
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A man hiding his annoyance when plans go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' is the container signal; the surface's man hiding his feelings disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitches are snags or problems that stop things going smoothly.

clue.text: Having given me a kiss, I can identify nationality!

parts.note: X is the conventional written kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A kiss from someone gives away where they come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexican names a person's nationality, someone from Mexico.

clue.text: You'll find it in the kitchen sink, love

definitions.text: You'll find it in the kitchen

parts.note: to sag is to sink or droop
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sentimental note about the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitchen sink' looks like a set phrase; 'sink' is wordplay and 'kitchen' ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch used for puddings, a store-cupboard staple.

clue.text: Like a fruitcake and biscuits?

definitions.meaning: fruitcake is slang for a mad person, so this means insane
thin dry savoury biscuits, often eaten with cheese

explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is slang for mad and also the name of thin crisp biscuits.

clue.text: Ridiculously proud, about to have big fall

indicators.note: about means going round another piece
ridiculously suggests the letters arranged absurdly

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: An arrogant person heading for a humiliating fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ridiculously' scrambles the pride into DPOUR, and 'about' wraps that round the possession; the proverb about pride before a fall disguises the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is a heavy fall of rain.

clue.text: Plane trips going to see shifty foreigner

indicators.note: trips as in stumbles, the letters of plane tumbling into a new order
shifty suggests the letters of see shifting position

explanation.surface: Air travel to visit a suspicious outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' rearranges PLANE to NEPAL; 'shifty' rearranges SEE to ESE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepalese person comes from Nepal, a foreigner to the British setter.

clue.text: Bird seeking a mate?

definitions.meaning: a black bird of the crow family
a chess piece, the castle, which hunts for checkmate

explanation.walkthrough: The courting bird is a red herring: the mate is checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is both a crow-like bird and the chess castle that helps deliver checkmate.

clue.text: Traumatised and frightened right to the core

indicators.note: to the core sends one letter right into the middle of another word

parts.note: scared means frightened

explanation.surface: Someone shaken through and through by fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the core' places R in the middle of SCARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mentally damaged by an ordeal is left with lasting emotional marks.

clue.text: Prepared to bolt, given a chance

definitions.text: Prepared to bolt, given a chance

parts.words: Prepared to bolt, given a chance
parts.note: bolt here means wolf down food, as a ravenous person would

explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' suggests running away, but here it is gulping food.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravenous person would gobble a meal quickly if offered one.

clue.text: Women's focal point when joining is to complain!

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
a hinge is the pivot on which a joint turns

explanation.surface: A woman's central moan when she joins a group.
explanation.definitionFit: To whinge is British slang for to moan or grumble.

clue.text: Extracts from 'Holidays' read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud means we want a word sounding the same

parts.note: rests are breaks or holidays

explanation.surface: Quoting passages from a book titled Holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extracts' looks like a noun for passages; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest something is to pull it away forcibly.

clue.text: Problem with ice creams that bear eats up

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the cones hold another piece within

parts.note: cones are ice creams served in wafer cones
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A dessert dilemma: a bear gobbling ice creams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that bear' makes CONES carry SUM; 'bear' looks like the animal but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to eat it up.

clue.text: Fight with female inside ring

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another

parts.note: war is fighting on a large scale
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman boxer fighting in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the boxing ring but is a flat washer.
explanation.definitionFit: A washer is a flat ring fitted under a nut or bolt.

clue.text: A crack up leaves one not right in the head

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a crack is a joke, like a gag

explanation.surface: A joke falls flat and leaves someone looking dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A GAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for senile or mentally confused.

clue.text: One recoils with 'Yuk! No more!'

indicators.note: to recoil is to spring back, so the word one is read backwards

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust like yuk

explanation.surface: Someone shrinking back in disgust and refusing any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoils' turns ONE into ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as an exclamation, it means stop, that is sufficient.

clue.text: Shows about how old trousers will be

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the trousers go round the other piece

parts.note: pants is the American word for trousers
age tells how old someone is

explanation.surface: Displays that comment on how long trousers will last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; American trousers are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageants are grand public spectacles or processions.

clue.text: S-speaks to the highest authority to get flowers

parts.note: the stammered first letter supplies an S
praying is addressing God, the highest authority

explanation.surface: A stammering petitioner addresses the top for blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter on 'S-speaks' gives an extra S before PRAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprays are small bunches of cut blossoms on a stem.

clue.text: Of indeterminate age, not popular with the opposite sex

definitions.text: not popular with the opposite sex
definitions.meaning: lacking a romantic partner to go out with

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a date means both timeless and having no romantic partner.
